message: Use British English. Always ask before deploying.
From now on, write commit messages in the imperative mood. Keep each subject line under 60 characters.
Always cite file paths with line numbers. Never paste whole files into your replies.
Going forward, prefer pnpm over npm in this repo. Pin every new dependency to an exact version.
Default to metric units in examples. Round currency to two decimals. Show dates as YYYY-MM-DD.
Always run the linter before you propose a patch. Also, from now on, add a test for every bug you fix.
Never rewrite history on shared branches. Always open a pull request for changes to the CI workflows.
For all future reviews, list blocking issues first. Keep nitpicks in a separate section at the end.
Never add emojis to documentation. Use sentence case for every heading from now on.
Answer in Spanish by default. Keep code identifiers in English.
Apply the schema change to the test database now. Going forward, take a snapshot before every schema change.
Can you check why the build failed? Also, always include the failing command in bug reports.
From now on, use tabs in Go files. Please fix the import order in server.go. Never commit generated mocks.
Here is the log from last night. Always summarize logs before quoting them.
Rename the helper to parseConfig. Keep function names in camelCase from here on.
From now on, write the changelog entry before the code. Bump the version for this release now.
Thanks for the fix. For future answers, keep explanations under five sentences.
Review this diff for me. Use bullet points in every review from now on. Also check the tests.
Always run the full test suite before committing, unless the change only touches documentation.
From now on, reply in English except when I write to you in French.
Never deploy on Fridays unless I explicitly approve it in the chat.
Use four-space indentation everywhere, except in Makefiles, which need tabs.
By default, squash commits when merging, unless the branch is a release branch.
Keep replies short from now on unless I ask for detail.
Always run the full test suite before pushing. The only exception is a docs-only change.
Never merge without a review. If it is an urgent security fix, one approval from me is enough.
From now on, write all examples in TypeScript. Shell snippets are fine for install steps.
Default to UTC in logs. Local time is allowed only in user-facing messages.
Fix the failing test in parser.ts. Then push the branch and open a draft PR.
What does the retry flag do? Is it safe to set it to zero?
If we always deployed on Mondays, would the pager load drop? Just curious, no change needed.
The style guide says 'always use semicolons'. Can you check whether this file follows it?
My teammate told me to never use default exports. What do you think about that advice?
Run the benchmarks now. Always use the release build for this run.
For this task only, skip the integration tests. Just run the unit tests and report back.
Please summarize the incident report. Keep it under 200 words.
Here is the error output. It always fails on the second request.
Let's try the other approach. Revert my last change and rebuild.
Imagine a rule that every commit must be signed. How would you enforce it in CI?
Thanks, that worked. Can you close the ticket now?
Push the hotfix branch now. Then tag the build.

rules.text: Name branches after the ticket key.
Keep pull request descriptions to one screen.
Use imperial units in examples.
Prefer composition over inheritance in new classes.
Write dates as MM/DD/YYYY.
Put feature flags behind a single config module.
Mark flaky tests with a tracking link.
Order imports alphabetically.
Explain every regex with a short comment.
Avoid abbreviations in public API names.
Log errors with a request identifier.
Return early instead of nesting conditionals.
Keep migrations reversible.
Add a screenshot to every UI pull request.
Prefix internal helpers with an underscore.
Store secrets only in the vault.
Run the formatter before staging changes.
Mention breaking changes in the release notes.
Cap line length at one hundred characters.
Group related constants in one file.
Write docstrings for exported functions.
Close stale branches after a month.
Prefer async iterators for streaming reads.
Benchmark hot paths before optimizing them.
Keep fixtures small and deterministic.
Tag releases with signed tags.
Review dependency licenses before adding packages.
Document every environment variable in the README.
Retry network calls with jittered backoff.
Pin the toolchain version in CI.
Squash fixup commits before review.
Link design documents from the pull request.
Prefer table-driven tests for parsers.
Keep error messages actionable.
Profile memory before raising limits.
Validate inputs at the boundary.
Archive old dashboards instead of deleting them.
Translate user-facing strings through the catalog.
Keep cron schedules in one manifest.
Rotate service tokens every quarter.
